## What is generated

`wiki/world.json` and every page in `wiki/places/`, `wiki/resources/`, `wiki/services/` and `wiki/training/`
are written by `bun run world` (`wiki/world/build.ts`) from `server/content`, the curated areas and the curated
methods (`wiki/world/methods.ts`); then, from the world it just built, the npc, shop and item pages in `wiki/npcs/`,
`wiki/shops/` and `wiki/items/` (and their sections of `wiki/README.md` when it exists). All are committed with
the code. Never edit them by hand: the next build overwrites the edit, and `bun wiki/world/build.ts --check` (part
of `bun run verify:conductor`) fails while a page differs from a fresh build, is missing, or is an extra `.md` in
one of those seven folders. The build also deletes pages it no longer renders from them (a folder's `README.md`
aside in the last three).

A site's stand tile is the first candidate a walk reaches with no requirement, else the first it reaches at all
(`SiteOptions.free`): a sandbar behind a key is no stand when a free tile exists. A fishing site's candidates are
the walkable tiles beside any tile its spots move to (its enum's tiles and the spawns, `SiteOptions.moves`), as
`place.ts` `besideSpot` has them for the `stand` check too (spot tiles are water, so these share an edge with one,
not across a wall: a diagonal would count only beside an open tile), nearest
the centre of their cover, so a pool spawned at one end of its enum stands by the middle; its nearest sinks are
priced from that stand.

A site is a cluster of same-kind features (locs or npc spawns) in one area: its id is
`kind:area:n`, its centre the mean tile, its stand tile a walkable tile beside it, a walk's first.
An npc whose approach ops widen their range (`if (npc_range(coord) > n) { p_aprange(n); ... }`,
`approachRange` in `sources/triggers.ts`) may also be stood for from any tile within that range in
sight of it, as the engine takes an approach op: the Burthorpe Games Room barmaid is traded with across
her bar. The collision data has no sight flags, so a line of sight there is a line of walk with the locs
that block walking but not sight (`blockrange=no`, the bar's pumps) cleared. Coordinates are `(x, z)`,
with ` L<n>` above level 0; underground areas sit at z + 6400.

Every table of sites (the resource, service, place and npc pages) gives each site's Box, the box its features'
tiles span (`x x1-x2, z z1-z2`; one tile as its coord), a Roam where its npcs walk (the box grown by their wander,
`Site.roam`), and an Area to copy: the plan `area` (`{ x, z, radius }`, conductor `AreaSchema`) that covers every
tile of the roam, or of the box where there is none (`cover.ts`): the box's centre, and the straight-line distance
to its farthest corner rounded up plus `COVER_MARGIN` (3) tiles, as a plan's area holds what is within its radius
of the centre in a straight line (`conductor/lib/area.ts` `inArea`). A fishing site's Area to copy points to its
Movement on its resource page, whose cover is the same over every tile its spots move to. Size a gathering `area`
from that cell, never from the centre and a guessed radius: a tight area idles the bot while a target stands just
outside it, and a wide one costs only a few tiles of walking.

`npcSpawns` in world.json clusters every placed npc's spawns the same way, per config, whether or
not a feature kind takes it. The npc pages (`wiki/generate-npcs.ts`) read their Locations from it
and from the sites, and the shop pages (`wiki/generate-shops.ts`) their Coordinates from the shop
sites; the item pages (`wiki/generate-items.ts`) read their drops from the npc pages. `bun run world`
runs the three in that order on the world in memory, so a check sees fresh pages. Run alone
(`bun wiki/generate-<x>.ts`), npcs and shops refuse a world.json built from other game data, and items
reads the npc pages on disk.

Each cluster, and each site whose features are all npcs (a pickpocket or npc site, not a bank whose booths
are locs), says how its npcs move (`sources/npc-movement.ts`, from the `.npc` configs and the engine's
defaults in `NpcType.ts`): `wander`, the Chebyshev tiles past its spawns an npc walks on its own (its
`wanderrange` when its `defaultmode` wanders and its `moverestrict` is not `nomove`, else 0; for a patrol,
how far its patrol coords reach past the spawns); `roam`, the `bbox` grown by `wander`; `respawnTicks`, the
config's `respawnrate`; and `moves`, the first `npc_tele` or `npc_changetype` an ai trigger of its own (or its
category's) runs, by any depth of calls: imps teleport, Canifis citizens turn into werewolves. A cluster of
several configs takes the largest wander, the fastest respawn and any move. `bbox` stays the spawns' box, so
stand tiles and a method's site lookup do not move with it.

## Reach and requirements

A site's `reach` in world.json is what a walk from the Lumbridge spawn needs to get to its stand tile
(`wiki/world/reach.ts`, `reachGraph` then `fillReach`), joined with a quest that locks the use of its locs
(`USE_GATES` in `gates.ts`: the Doric and Rellekka anvils, the Rellekka furnaces and spinning wheel): its minimal requirement
sets, `[[]]` for none and `[]` when no walk gets there. An npc cluster's `reach` is that of the tiles beside it,
wherever it has wandered to, as a bot talks to an npc from beside it (`besideCluster` in `place.ts`: the tiles of
its roam that steps from its spawns get to with every door shut, as an npc opens none, and the ring round them a
wall does not cut off). The fill keeps at most `MAX_SETS` (24) sets per tile.

The pages show it in a Requires column: `-` for none, the sets joined with "or", `unreached`, or `no stand`
for a site with no stand tile; so a `-` row on a service or resource page is one a fresh account can walk to and use.
Within a set every requirement applies; any one set is enough. A set is written in the token forms of
`wiki/world/requirements.ts` (its header lists them):

| Token | Means |
|---|---|
| `quest:<id>`, `quest:<id>>=<stage>` | the quest is done; the quest has reached a stage (completion meets it) |
| `skill:<skill>:<level>`, `questpoints:<n>` | a base level; at least n quest points |
| `item:<obj>:worn\|held`, `category:<category>:worn\|held` | wearing or carrying the obj, or any obj of a category |
| `coins:<n>`, `consume:<obj>:<n>` | taken per crossing: a toll or fare, a pass or ticket |
| `members` | a members world |
| `loadout:<id>` | carrying none of a loadout rule's categories (Entrana: no weapons or armour) |
| `other:<text>` | a condition none of the forms fit; the build report lists each |
| `other:came from <npc>` | the way came in by the npc's teleport: a way out back to where it came from (the essence mine's portals) |

Sets are canonical (`canonicalSet`, `dominates`): a requirement another in the set implies is merged away
(`quest:x` covers `quest:x>=3`), the coins of every crossing on the way are summed into one `coins:<n>`, a
`consume` is summed per obj, and a set another set's requirements all imply is dropped. So a set that reads
`coins:10` has one toll on its way and `coins:20` two.

Resource and processor sites also carry `nearest` (`wiki/world/distance.ts`): the nearest bank, and for ore,
raw fish and smelted bars the nearest furnace, range or anvil, each as the sink site's id, the run ticks from the
site's stand tile to the sink's, and what that way needs, under the site's own `reach` sets. Distances are
run ticks only, because bots always run; a crossing (a stair, a gate, a ship, a cart, a sled, a scripted move, a
teleport) costs a fixed `CROSSING_TICKS` for its kind, an estimate, plus what its row adds (below). The pages show it in a
Nearest bank column (`none` when no bank is reached that way).

Where the ways come from: connectors (stairs, ladders, trapdoors, manholes, gangplanks) are read from
`scripts/ladders+stairs/` (`sources/connectors.ts`); gates from the scan of the scripts' door and gate triggers
(`sources/gate-scan.ts`), each confirmed or rejected in `gate-list.ts` (exported by `gates.ts`); transports
(ships, carts, sleds) from the sail scripts (`sources/transports.ts`) plus `CURATED_TRANSPORTS` in `gates.ts` (the
Miscellania longship among them, whose own sail proc sets no journey); scripted crossings from the loc op moves no
gate row makes (`deriveScriptedMoves` in `sources/gate-landings.ts`, below); teleports to a dbrow's coords from
`DBROW_TELEPORTS` in `gates.ts` (`sources/dbrow-teleports.ts`, below), and the curated teleports and moves of
`CURATED_CROSSINGS` (`sources/curated-crossings.ts`, below).
Every curated entry cites its script, and the build fails on a candidate nobody reviewed. The doors the collision
data lists are walked through as the walker opens them; its list has no diagonal (shape 9) door, so every placed
one the plain door script opens is in `EXTRA_DOORS` (`conductor/actions/paths.ts`), shared by the walker and the
fill, and `test/collision.real.test.ts` fails on one left out.

### The crossing model

`crossings` in world.json (`Crossing` in `types.ts`) holds the moves no connector, gate or transport row describes:
`scripted` (a loc op that moves the player with no condition the gate scan decides) and `teleport` (an item used on a
loc, an npc's op and dialogue, an item op, an interface click). A row says how the move is done (`act`: `loc-op`,
`item-on-loc`, `npc-op` with its dialogue `choices`, `item-op` or `interface`), the loc or npc it is done on (`at`),
the tiles it is done from (`from`), where it lands (`landings`: one tile, or the set a random landing draws from),
its requirement sets, and its `roll` when the move is behind a `stat_random`. A connector's and a gate's act is
implied by their rows (the loc's op, the trigger), but a gate row whose move is behind dialogue carries one with its
`choices` (`gate-list.ts`): the Shantay Pass's poster, which the script asks only of a player holding no disclaimer,
is answered when shown. A transport may carry one, and the sail and curated rows carry none. A gate row may carry a
`roll` too.

The gate scan and every bound run follow a `queue`, `strongqueue`, `weakqueue` or `longqueue` the trigger issues that
queues a moving `[queue,name]` script: it runs once the trigger's script ends, however it ended, and its moves are
the trigger's, under every condition the path took. That is the Shantay Pass's way in: its gate row lands each north
stand south of the pass under `consume:shantay_pass:1` (the `inv_del` before the queue), so the desert behind it is
reached. The engine runs queued scripts in the order queued within the main queue list, as delays allow; the weak
queue runs after it. The walker runs them in the order queued, which differs only where one has a delay or a
weakqueue comes before another queue, and follows a weakqueue as if it ran (the engine drops one when a modal closes
or the active script resumes); the build report lists each moving script queued with a delay or on the weak queue. A
queued script has no active loc, so its loc commands leave the trigger's loc as it was. A death's respawn
(`[queue,player_death]`) is not passage, nor is a move only through one (a `damage_player` queue).

A gate row with `from` checks the move only from that side, and a curated `oneWay` gate gives no edge from the other,
where its script refuses the player (the castle crumbly wall, `skill_agility/scripts/shortcuts.rs2:6`). A one-sided
gate on an object counts a stand level with the loc on its checked side (`standOnSide` in `reach.ts`), but the scripts
disagree (the Shantay Pass and the Barbarian Outpost pipe let a level stand through free, the Khazard low wall does
not). So a gate row's landing is `free` when the bound run finds a path from that stand that needs nothing (unless
every landing of the row is: no path the run took then reads its requirement), and the fill crosses it free whatever
its side: the Shantay Pass's east stand goes out free, and the desert mine's nearest bank (the pass's bank chest)
needs only the camp's key. A path past a condition the bound run can't read (an npc nearby) is not free, but for a
wait: a var compared with `map_clock` the way the clock opens, an obstacle someone used a few ticks ago (the agility
pipes, the lumberyard fence); the build report lists each free landing reached past one. A move onto a tile of the
row's own loc, which blocks it (the Lumber Yard's broken fence climbed from the south), leaves the player there to
walk off, so it lands on each tile of walkable land a step from that tile goes to; the build report lists each.

The `scripted` rows are the moves of the loc op triggers the gate scan finds moving the player with no condition it
reads before the move, and of the temporary blocks (the Gnome Stronghold gate), outside the connector scripts: each is
run, as a gate row's trigger is, for every placed loc of an op its config has and every tile on land it is used from
(`gateLander`). A stand gives a row when its move lands on walkable land the stand could not walk to in a few steps
(a passage, not a shuffle beside the loc, a stay put or a door's swing), on one tile; stands landing alike make one free
row, `act: loc-op`. A `stat_random` roll on the way is followed both ways: the failed paths give the row's `roll`, their
delays' ticks, the most damage they deal (a stat read as 99, a random draw at its top) and the tile they leave the
player on, unless that tile is a short walk from the landing (the failure gets the player across all the same). Gate
rows with a skill requirement get their roll the same way. What no run settles (a `map_findsquare` landing, a coord kept
in a varp, a stand landing on two passages) is listed in the build report, never guessed; stands stopped only in the
door procs (`doors/scripts/`) are a door's, which the collision data or `gate-list.ts` has. A move on a loc tile and op
that has a connector row is refused, and the build fails on one. A call of a proc that only sets locals and returns
a value is that value, a coord computed from the player's tile marked so: the Haunted Mine's ladders
(`~setcoord_mapsquare`, the stand's own tile in another mapsquare) settle that way.

The runecrafting ruins and their temples' exit portals are `DBROW_TELEPORTS` rows: the trigger's dbrow row, found by
the loc's `rune_type`, gives the landing coords and the talisman, which the gate scan does not read. Each placed
ruins gets a `teleport` row, `act: item-on-loc` with its talisman and `item:<talisman>:held` (and `members` on a
members row), and each portal a free `scripted` row back out. A row lands on every tile its coords can give: one of
several coords (the cosmic temple's four entrances, the chaos portals' eight tiles round the ruins), and with a
radius (`map_findsquare`, the body temple's) any open tile of the coord's ring with a line of walk to the coord. Ten altars are reached this way; the
death temple has no ruins in this revision, so its altar is in `EXPECTED_UNREACHED`, and so are the decoration trees
round the air, nature and water temples that no walk from the landing gets beside.

The rune essence mine is an `NPC_TELEPORTS` entry: every npc op trigger whose whole body jumps to
`@teleport_to_essence_mine` (Aubury's op4; Sedridor's, Cromperty's, Distentor's and Brimstail's op3) gets a
`teleport` row, `act: npc-op`, done from the tiles beside the wizard's spawn, under `quest:runemysteries`, landing on
every tile the `essence_mine_teleports` draw can give (each coord, and the open tiles within 1 with a line of sight to
it). The portals send the player back to the wizard they came by, which a varp keeps and no stateless edge follows,
so each portal has a row to every wizard's exit (the open tiles within 2 with a line of walk to it), under
`other:came from <npc>` and what gets a walk to that wizard's teleport, read off a fill without the portals:
Distentor's adds 66 Magic, as he stands inside the Magic Guild. A site's nearest-sink search meets every came-from
requirement (`NearestOptions.context`), so the mine's rocks have a bank (Varrock East, by a portal to Aubury), and a
fill takes a portal only where a walk already gets, so no reach set asks a came-from. A few landings are nooks the
cave walls and dead trees close in, which no walk leaves: they are stranded (below), so they get no spread and the
build report lists them, and every other landing of a wizard's row is priced to its farthest among the rest.

The moves the derivations don't give are `CURATED_CROSSINGS` rows, each checked against its script
(`sources/curated-crossings.ts`): the trigger's header is in the scripts, each landing (or a constant naming it) is
written in the trigger's script or on the move's line, each dialogue choice is an option text there, each zone is an
`inzone` the scripts check, and for a loc or npc op trigger the gate scan finds the move to each landing. They are
Monkey Madness's rides (Daero to the glider hangar for a player past the quest's training, Waydar's glider to Crash
Island and back, Lumdo's boat to Ape Atoll and back, each npc's rows by the zone its script checks `npc_coord`
against), the spirit trees (a row per menu choice), the gnome gliders (a row per start and button, each landing a
`map_findsquare` ring), the Fisher Realm's whistle (an item op done on the zone's tiles; the way back from the realm
land a walk from the landing gets to) and the Burthorpe Games Room stairs (every tile of their random draw). A landing
the script puts on a tile the collision blocks (the whistle's, inside an oak) lands on the tiles the player steps out
to, and the build report lists it.

The fill adds an edge from every `from` tile to every landing, under the row's alternatives. The build prices the rows
over the graph (`priceCrossings` in `distance.ts`) and writes the prices on them:

- a landing's `spread`: the run ticks to it from the row's landing farthest from it. The edge to that landing costs
  the crossing plus its spread, so a random landing counts as its longest one: a way on from any landing costs at
  least what it would from the worst, and exactly that when the landings are close together. A landing is stranded
  when no walk from it gets to the row's largest group of landings that each walk to the other, and that group holds
  most of the row's landings on land (`strandedLandings`): no walk takes it to the rest, so it gets no spread, the
  others' spreads leave it out, and the build report lists it;
- a roll's `fail.back`: the run ticks from the tile a failure leaves the player on back to the nearest tile the move
  is tried from (0 when a failure leaves them where they tried). A rolled edge costs its expected ticks, the success
  plus (1 - p)/p times the failure's ticks and the way back, with p the engine's `stat_random` chance (`roll.ts`) at
  the lowest level the row's requirement allows.

Both are walks over the neighbour steps and the free edges that carry no price of their own. A landing or a way back
no walk gets to is left unpriced and listed in the build report, and the distances do not take that edge (the fill
still does). The conductor's walker (`conductor/lib/walk-graph.ts`) walks scripted moves and teleports, and prices a
roll at the bot's own level rather than the lowest allowed; it does not take transports, nor a crossing its `cross`
can't make (`crossingRefusal`: an interface click, the gliders', whose interface the row names no op to open).

An `act` is one op, with its dialogue choices. It can't say a move of two loc ops in turn (the Legends' Quest winch:
once a rope is tied on, op1 turns the bare winch into the roped one, whose op1 climbs down) or a spell cast on a loc
(an `oploct` trigger: Charge Orb on the quest's magic trial gate), so the Legends' Quest cavern behind them is in
`EXPECTED_UNREACHED` though players get there. Nor can it say an opener before the act: a glider row is its interface
button alone, so the walker leaves the gliders out until an act can carry what opens the interface first (the pilot's
op and dialogue).

### The unreached report

`bun run world` prints, after the build, a warning listing every site of a covered kind (bank, shop, resource,
service) that no walk from the Lumbridge spawn reaches, grouped by pocket. A pocket is the land a flood from
one such site gets to over neighbour steps and the graph's edges without entering a reached tile; sites the
same flood gets to share it, most sites first. Each pocket gives its areas, its size in tiles, the nearest
reached tile to any of its sites (on that site's plane), its sites by kind, and its hints: every loc op (an op
the loc's config has, or use-item) and npc op with a trigger, placed on or one tile beside the pocket, with the
trigger's script line and what the gate scan made of it: a gate candidate and its kind (from `gate-list.ts`, or
the scan's proposal for an npc op), an unconditional move, or no move found (these last on one line). A flood
that takes 32768 tiles stops and calls its pocket open: a large unreached landmass, or an upper floor or an
instanced room whose empty tiles round it the collision data lists as walkable land; its hints are only
those of the tiles taken.

It is warnings only; `--check` leaves it out. Work it as a curation to-do list, a pocket at a time: read its
hints' scripts, then either add the missing connector, gate or transport (the derivation in
`wiki/world/sources/`, or a row in `gate-list.ts` / `gates.ts`), or, when nobody playing walks there, add an
entry to `EXPECTED_UNREACHED` in `areas.ts` (an area, its child areas included, or one site, with a reason and
the script line that keeps the player out). The report leaves those sites out, and the build fails on an entry
that names no such area or site, and on one no unreached site matches, so an entry goes once its sites are
reached or gone. A site walled in by collision, with no loc or npc op on or beside its pocket that moves the player
but its own, cites the op it is used by (`woodcut.rs2:1` for a tree), whose reach test no tile a walk gets to passes,
and its reason names a loc or map flag that walls it with the map square line (`hedge at maps/m45_54.jm2:5352`).
One entry's reason may cover several sites walled in alike (the decoration trees of the Feldip Hills behind its
railings and dry stone walls). Before adding an entry, read the hints on and beside its pocket to confirm none
moves the player, or, when one does but the index can't model it, name that crossing in the reason.

The table also holds the pockets players do get into by a crossing the index misses (the Kharazi jungle's cuts,
the Dwarf Cannon cave, the Regicide pit traps, the desert mining camp's mine, the fishing platform, parts of the
Underground Pass, and more): each reason names the crossing and cites its script line, and
`conductor/roadmap.md` (Review follow-ups) tracks deriving them. An entry goes stale, and fails the build, once
its crossing is derived and its sites are reached, so it is removed with the derivation.

The fill's own warning before it, the rows it could not use, says why each is left out: a landing not on land (a
middle ladder on the top level), a wall whose side the row can't read, or a gate row with no derived landing, with
what stopped the derivation (no tile on land reaches the loc, every landing off walkable land, a construct not
known offline).

A curated table names a site by a `SiteKey` (`site-key.ts`), never by its id: `{ kind, at }`, the site of that
kind holding a feature on the tile `at` (`siteAt('tree', 2166, 3091)`; the report prints it as
`tree (2166, 3091, 0)`). A site id (`tree:kandarin:7`) is an ordinal within its kind and leaf area, so a change to
the clustering or the areas renumbers it, and an entry naming it would silently name another site. A feature
belongs to exactly one site whatever happens to the others, where a site's bbox can overlap others', so a tile of
one names it. Take any of the site's features' tiles from `world.json`; the build fails on a key no site of its
kind holds, or several do. `EXPECTED_UNREACHED`, the build checks' allowlists in `allow.ts` and the bank
`OVERRIDES` in `conductor/lib/banks.ts` are keyed so; ids stay in `world.json` and on the pages.

### Build checks

`checks.ts` holds checks for classes of wrong data the index audit found (`conductor/docs/world-index-data-audit.md`
§2.2). Each returns findings naming their sites by `SiteKey` (`unclaimed` its configs, below) with a detail line; its allowlist in `allow.ts` lists
the findings known and explained, each entry `{ keys, reason, source }`: the keys of the finding's sites, what is
wrong and what fixes it, and a map line (`maps/mX_Z.jm2:line`) of a feature or the script line of the op that
settles it. `bun run world` and `--check` print a `checks:` line per check and fail with `ERROR <check>:` lines on
a finding no entry allows, an entry whose key names no one site (invalid), and an entry no finding matches (stale:
the rect it waited on was refitted, or the site is gone; or it repeats an earlier entry's match), so an entry goes when its fix lands. `near-miss` and
`split` look at the COVERED kinds but trees, whose sites chain whole forests; `stand` at every site with a stand
some walk reaches.

- **`unclaimed`** (`UNCLAIMED_ALLOW`): a config the maps place with an op trigger (op, approach or use-item) that no
  classify rule made a feature through (`classify.ts` `Classification.unclaimed`: an attackable npc's kind claims
  only its Attack ops, so a cow's Milk is unclaimed), whose body or the labels and procs it calls (`reach`, as
  classify follows them) has a gather or processing shape (`checks.ts` `SHAPES`): a `stat_advance` of a stat but
  agility, one of agility on a config the reach graph has no crossing by (`crossedConfigs`: a loc or npc of
  `World.crossings` or a loc of `World.gates`; a crossed obstacle's xp is the crossing's), `~openshop`, `inv_add`
  with a `loc_change`/`loc_del`/`npc_changetype` in one body or with a `p_delay`/`anim` while a body runs the op
  again (`p_oploc`, `p_opnpc`), `~pickup_loc_floor`, or a use-item op that takes the item (`inv_del`) and gives one
  or animates. Ops labelled Talk-to are left out, and an npc's labelled Attack (a loc's, a training dummy's, is a
  use), and a bare `inv_add` is no shape: dialogue handing out a quest item would flood the list (audit B1, B2, C).
  One finding per config, `loc <config>` or `npc <config>`, naming each trigger's `file:line`. An entry is
  `{ configs, reason, source }`: one config or a group sharing the reason, with one's trigger line as the source; it
  is invalid when it names no config or one no map places, and stale for each config it names that no finding is
  about; one naming a config an earlier entry names is a stale duplicate, naming the configs they share. The report
  counts the findings each reason allows. **The entries whose reason names a kind (`well: 2.6`, `crop: 2.6`,
  `mill: 2.6`, ...) are plan 2.6's to-do list**: adding the kind or fixing the rule makes the entry stale, and it
  goes. The other reasons say why the config is no feature (a quest one-off, a minigame, a door, a repeatable use
  with no kind 2.6 plans), and an uncrossed agility obstacle's why the build has no crossing for it.
- **`near-miss`** (`NEAR_MISS_ALLOW`): a site whose bbox lies outside every rect of a leaf area (one no area is the
  parent of) on its level, but 1-3 tiles (Chebyshev) from one, while its own leaf area is another: usually a rect
  drawn as a label square and never fitted to the place, with the site filed under the parent instead. A leaf drawn
  round one thing (a bank's booths, a resource, a course) beside a site of the town around it is a near miss by
  design; its entry says so.
- **`split`** (`SPLIT_ALLOW`): two sites of one kind holding a feature of the same config, in different leaf areas,
  with a feature of each within the kind's `SITE_RADIUS` of the other on one level: `place.ts` links any two
  features of a kind that close, but only within one leaf area, so they are one place clustered as two because an
  area edge cuts it. An entry names both sites.
- **`stand`** (`STAND_ALLOW`): a site whose stand is cut off from it (audit E4). Its stand's free walk (steps, and
  crossings that need nothing, within the rect holding the site's roam, or its bbox when it has none, every use
  tile and the stand, grown by twice the kind's `SITE_RADIUS`) gets to a use tile of fewer than half its members: a
  loc's `reachTiles`, the walkable tiles beside an npc's roam (`besideCluster`), and for a fishing spot those beside
  any tile of its subtype's `movement`. The stand is a tile of the walk like any other: on an opened loc asking
  something, the walk gets nothing. A member no walk gets to a use tile of (a duck mid-pond, a banker behind the
  counter) is left out of the count. A site wandering more than 64 tiles (`MAX_WANDER`) is not walked, its bound
  being the map, and is a finding of its own (`wanders N > MAX_WANDER 64, not walked`). Or the kind takes its products to a bank
  (`distance.ts` `SINKS`) and the stand has no nearest bank, or one whose way asks more (`requirements.ts`
  `dominates`) than every member's own way in: its use tiles' sets joined with what using the site asks, as the
  site's reach joins them. A stand in the wrong pocket waits on the stand rework (audit §2.4); a place the graph
  has no priced way out of has no nearest bank from any stand, and its entry says what is missing.
- **`moving`** (`MOVING_ALLOW`): a fishing spot's movement enum feeding the features of two or more sites (one
  finding per enum, naming them), or a fishing site some of whose spots' tiles (`Site.movement`) lie in no rect of
  its leaf area on their level (one per site; a site in no area is left out), audit A1, A2. The shore join merges an
  enum's spots only within one leaf area and level, so an enum crossing an area edge is split, and an enum tile past
  the rect is a pool roaming out. Clustering across leaf areas (audit §2.4) or a rect refit (§2.5) removes one.

## Methods

A method is a curated record in `wiki/world/methods.ts` (`MethodDef`): a family (the kind of action: woodcutting,
mining, fishing, pickpocket, stall, cooking, combat; `model/families/`), a tile `at` in the gather site, the family's params,
a sink and the promoted plans that run it. The sink is `drop`, `bank`, or `process`: ordered steps, each a family and
its params at a tile, `'here'` (where the previous action stands) or, omitted, the nearest site of the family's kinds,
then `end: bank | drop | keep` for what the last step makes. The `withdraw` family (params `{ obj }`) is a source
instead of a gather: it takes the obj from the bank at `at`, and its process sink starts and ends there. Sites
renumber when the data changes and tiles don't, so a record names a tile. `bun run world` resolves each
(`model/method.ts`: its site, sinks, legs, minimum level) into `methods[]` in world.json and fails naming a record it
can't; there is no rate grid in world.json.

The **floor** (`model/cycle.ts`) is the tick-perfect rate of a method at a profile (levels, tool, food): the game's
formulas (`model/`, each citing its script) for ideal play over the shortest way, with no tick wasted and banking at
its minimum tick cost. Legs are run ticks. A bot measures at or below it, and the gap is what a tick-perfect pass
works on; a measured figure above its floor is a model bug. The pages in `wiki/training/` show the floor by level
beside the measured figures; `methodRate(id, profile, skill?)` and `bestMethods(skill, profile, { met, maxWilderness,
multiway, aggressive })` in `query.ts` give it to code, `bestMethods` ranked by floor XP/hr.

What a record can say, beyond a gather and a sink (the code is the reference; each is worked from its script):

- **Process steps** (`sink.steps`, in order; each takes a product of the gather or an earlier step, and a step whose
  input the profile doesn't make is skipped). `at` is `'here'` (where the previous action stands: superheat beside the
  rock, fletching where the log was cut), a tile in a site of the family's kinds, or omitted for the nearest site of its
  first kind to the previous step's. A family with no site kinds (firemaking) stops at its own tile, or `'here'`; what
  follows it names its tile. `end` is `bank` (the nearest bank of the last step's site, or `bank`'s tile), `drop` or
  `keep` (a stackable product: runes). A bank is never visited on `keep` or `drop`, so `bank` with them is an error.
- **Withdraw** is a source in place of a gather (`family: 'withdraw'`, params `{ obj }`, `at` in a bank): the load
  comes from the bank in no ticks of its own and the process sink starts and ends there, so it takes no `bank`.
- **Supplies.** A step's `consumes` after the first (the chained input) are its supplies: stackable ones take a slot
  each, non-stackable ones (bow strings) a slot per unit carried from the start of the trip, and a wearable one is worn
  (a ring of forging's charges). A step `'here'` that uses a non-stackable supply is done as each item is gathered
  (chop, cut, string, chop), so the strung bow takes the log's slot and the string's comes free (`asItGoes`,
  `model/cycle.ts`); a step away from the stand carries its supplies all trip.
- **Step timings** a family sets on its `ActionModel`: `batch` (inputs a product takes), `restart` (ticks a trip spends
  starting the step again, once it takes more than `upTo` actions: the anvil's Make 10), `start` (ticks once a trip,
  where the first action is later than the cadence: the spinning menu) and `perTick` (the most actions one tick runs,
  where an action takes no tick of its own: stringing).
- **Laps.** An `agility` method's one attempt is a whole lap of a course site (`model/families/agility.ts`): each
  obstacle's moves are its crossing rows and gate rows (`Gate.standTicks`: the success ticks by stand tile, the most
  being `Gate.ticks`), the falls of rolled moves priced in at the profile's hitpoints, and the lap is the cheapest round
  over the walks between obstacles. The family names those tile pairs (`Family.walks`), `method.ts` prices them under
  each way's reach set into `MethodWay.walks`, and the family picks. A course gate on the lap's skill (the Barbarian
  course's Agility 35) shows as a `skill:` token of the way. The Wilderness ridge gates are not an obstacle of the lap
  and are left out of its floor.
- **Food** (`MethodDef.food`) covers a family's `failDamage` (a pickpocket stun) and `damage` (a lap's falls, a
  kill's hits once calibrated: below), restocked at the bank.
- **Kills.** A `combat` record (melee: `model/families/combat.ts`, the formulas in `model/combat.ts`) has one kill of
  its npc a success: `params: { npc }` (omitted when the site has one kind), `area` (a radius around `at` that gathers
  the npc's spawns across sites), `gear` (its worn objs; a query's `Profile.worn` takes their slots one by one) and
  `loot` (`model/cycle.ts` Loot: stackables kept, bones buried, banked or left, other drops left unless `keep` names
  them). A kill is the expected swings at the weapon's attack rate plus the run to the nearest other spawn past the
  swing cooldown; the respawn caps the rate; the pickup, a bury's swing gap and each eat are priced. The style is no
  param: a record is rated for the queried skill on the style that suits it (`styleParams`: Attack accurate, Strength
  aggressive, Defence defensive, Hitpoints and Prayer the best of them), and trains the skills its weapon's styles
  give, Prayer too when it buries. An npc whose melee AI a script overrides is a ModelError. `ResolvedMethod.npcs`
  (max hit, the npcs that hunt and up to which combat level, the target's retreat, which the floor leaves out) and
  `areaHazard` feed `methodHazard` and `bestMethods`' `aggressive` filter. Ranged and Magic are not modelled yet.
- **The food gate.** A kill eats food only once its npc has a record in `CALIBRATIONS` (`methods.ts`): worker runs whose
  damage and fight ticks a kill agree with `killFigures` within `CALIBRATION_TOLERANCE` (25%), from
  `conductor/test/integration/smoke/combat-calibration.itest.ts` and `conductor/tools/combat-ledger.ts`. Until then it
  eats nothing, its trips end on a full inventory, and where the npc can hit its page says Food/hr uncalibrated: its XP/hr
  leaves out food trips. `test/combat-method.real.test.ts` holds each record to the model.
- **Worn items** are `Profile.worn` (obj config names: a staff of fire, a ring of forging), which a family reads;
  `Measured.worn` records what a measured run wore.
- **Use gates.** A site's reach also carries what using its feature asks (`USE_GATES` in `gates.ts`: Doric's anvil
  needs the Doric quest, Rellekka's furnaces, anvil and spinning wheel The Fremennik Trials), so a method's `ways` include it.
  `distance.ts`' nearest-sink figures don't read them: a record names its step sites rather than rely on `nearest`.
- **Random landings.** A method's legs price a crossing that lands on one of several tiles (the essence mine's
  teleports and portals) at the chance-weighted mean of the walks on from each landing, and a teleport at its script's
  delays (`model/legs.ts`); the rest of the index still prices them at the worst landing.

Measured figures are curated, not read at build time: when a goal finishes, `bun conductor/tools/stats.ts <bot>
--methods` prints the paste-ready `measured` entry (XP/hr, the levels and tool the runs started at, the objs they wore
and for a melee method every combat-level skill, bot, date, hours, the command), and the conductor pastes it into the
record. A plan names its method (`PlanDef.method`, see
`conductor/docs/plans.md`) and the record lists the plan back.

### Model gaps

- **Moving fishing spots.** A spot teleports to a random free tile of its `fishing_movement_enum` every 280 +
  random(250) ticks (`fishing_movement.rs2`), so a bot walks to wherever one stands now. The fishing family's
  floor assumes a spot is always at hand and charges no walk to the next one, so it is an upper bound; the
  availability (a spot's uptime on the tile in reach, the walk to the next) is not modelled. Each fishing-spot site
  carries the tiles its spots can stand on and a covering area (`Site.movement`, `sources/fishing-movement.ts` and
  `cover.ts`: the tiles' box's centre and a straight-line radius that reaches every tile with `COVER_MARGIN` (3)
  tiles of margin), shown under Movement on the resource page; a plan's `area` should be at least that. Spots sharing an enum are one site (`SiteOptions.shore`).

Adding a method:

1. Write the record in `methods.ts`: a tile in the site, the params, the sink, the plans.
2. A new kind of action needs a family module in `model/families/` (one file, its registry line in `index.ts`) with a
   test worked by hand from its script in `test/families.test.ts`.
3. `bun run world`; read the method's row in `wiki/training/<skill>.md`.
4. After bots have run it, paste the `stats.ts --methods` entry into `measured`.

## Where corrections go

| Wrong on a page | Fix it in |
|---|---|
| An area's name, extent, parent or notes; a site named after the wrong place | `wiki/world/areas.ts` |
| A loc or npc missing, or listed as the wrong kind or subtype | the rule table in `wiki/world/classify.ts` |
| Sites split or merged wrongly, or a bad stand tile | `wiki/world/place.ts` (`SITE_RADIUS`, the stand rules) |
| A page's layout or wording | `wiki/world/render/` |
| A door or gate and what it needs; a Requires cell, or a site reading unreached that a bot gets to | its row in `wiki/world/gate-list.ts` (exported by `gates.ts`), or the derivation in `wiki/world/sources/gate-scan.ts`; else an `EXPECTED_UNREACHED` entry in `areas.ts` saying why |
| A site just outside the area it is named after, or one place split into two sites at an area edge (`ERROR near-miss`, `ERROR split`) | the area's rects in `wiki/world/areas.ts`; a pair that is right as it is (a leaf round one thing, two places side by side) is an entry in `NEAR_MISS_ALLOW` or `SPLIT_ALLOW` in `wiki/world/allow.ts` saying why |
| A placed loc or npc whose gather or processing trigger no rule claims (`ERROR unclaimed`) | the rule in `wiki/world/classify.ts`, or a new kind (plan 2.6); a config that is no feature (a quest one-off, a minigame) is an entry in `UNCLAIMED_ALLOW` in `wiki/world/allow.ts` saying why, and one waiting on 2.6 an entry naming the kind |
| A fishing enum split over several sites, or a pool moving out of its area (`ERROR moving`) | the area's rects in `wiki/world/areas.ts`, or the shore join (`place.ts` `joinShores`); until then an entry in `MOVING_ALLOW` in `wiki/world/allow.ts` saying why, with the enum line as its source |
| A stand cut off from most of its site's members or from a bank (`ERROR stand`) | how stands are chosen (`place.ts` `standTile`), or a missing or unpriced way out in the sources; until then an entry in `STAND_ALLOW` in `wiki/world/allow.ts` saying what cuts it off |
| A site whose use (not the walk there) needs a quest: a Requires cell missing it | `USE_GATES` in `wiki/world/gates.ts` |
| A transport (ship, cart, sled) or its fare | `CURATED_TRANSPORTS` in `wiki/world/gates.ts`, or `wiki/world/sources/transports.ts` |
| A teleport or move from npc dialogue, a menu, an item op or an interface (Monkey Madness's rides, spirit trees, gliders, the Fisher Realm's whistle) | `CURATED_CROSSINGS` in `wiki/world/gates.ts` (`sources/curated-crossings.ts`) |
| A staircase, ladder or trapdoor missing, or with the wrong landing | `wiki/world/sources/connectors.ts` (the scripts give landings; there is no table to patch) |
| A bank a task must never pick as nearest, or its stand tile | `OVERRIDES` in `conductor/lib/banks.ts`, keyed by a `SiteKey` |
| A connector's name or hazard note, or a connector the conductor's walker leaves out | `OVERRIDES` and `LEFT_OUT` in `conductor/lib/connectors.ts` (the rows themselves are generated from world.json) |
| A method's tile, params, sink, plans or a measured figure | its record in `wiki/world/methods.ts`, then `bun run world` |
| A method's floor (a formula, a cycle or tool rule) | the family module in `wiki/world/model/families/`, or `model/` (`cycle.ts`, `rate.ts`, `roll.ts`), with its hand-worked test |
| A kill's floor: hit chance, max hit, swings, damage taken, an npc's stats, styles or bonuses, drops | `wiki/world/model/combat.ts`, `model/families/combat.ts`, `model/npcs.ts`, `model/items.ts`, `sources/droptables.ts`, with a hand-worked test |
| A kill's Food/hr (the food gate) | a calibration run (`conductor/test/integration/smoke/combat-calibration.itest.ts`), then its record in `CALIBRATIONS` in `wiki/world/methods.ts` |

Then run `bun run world` and commit the code with the regenerated files. What is learned in game
about a place (a hazard, a route, a rate measured) goes in `learnings/` per the `knowledge` skill,
naming the page.
